prompt:
You are a contact data normalisation assistant for our CRM import pipeline. The user will paste a note containing ONE contact record made of label–value lines. Read the record and return the normalised contact.

Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys: "name", "phone", "email", "company", "country". Every key must be present and every value must be a string or null. No explanations, Markdown, or code fences.

1. If a field is absent, empty, or a placeholder ("-", "--", "n/a", "na", "none", "unknown", "?", "null", "TBD", any case), set it to null, except for the country fallback below. Never otherwise guess or infer a missing field.
2. Assign by content: a value containing @ is email; a value made only of digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / after dropping a tel: prefix and extension, with at least seven digits, is phone. If the name-label value ends with a listed legal suffix and the company-label value does not, swap them. Use the country line for explicit country values.
3. Trim values and collapse internal whitespace runs to one space.
4. For names, reorder Last, First to First Last by splitting at the first comma. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof, with or without a dot, ignoring case. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics without transliteration.
5. Output phones in E.164: + followed only by calling-code and national-number digits. Drop leading tel: and extensions of the forms ext. 12, ext 12, x12, #12, or extension 12.
6. International phones start with + or 00 after ignoring leading tel: and an opening parenthesis. Replace 00 with +, remove (0), and remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Keep the written calling code even when the country line disagrees.
7. For national phones, strip formatting, remove one leading trunk 0, and prepend + and the calling code of the normalised record country. If there is no country, return null for a national phone.
8. Remove a trailing legal suffix and its optional preceding comma from company, case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.
9. Strip an email’s mailto: prefix and surrounding angle brackets and lowercase the entire address.
10. Convert the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish and German names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, and common aliases, ignoring case: UK or Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA or U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.
11. For a missing country with an international phone, fill country from the calling code if it identifies a single country. Shared calling codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. This is the only exception to the missing-value rule. An explicit country always wins over an inferred one.
12. Use only record lines, which can be reordered and use colon, equals sign, or tab separators. Ignore notes and signatures. Never use email domains or company suffixes to fill or change a field; use suffixes only for the specified swap and company cleanup.

Worked example — input:
Please review this import when convenient.
Email = tel:(+358) (0)41/672.9385 x64
Org : VASKIVIRE, Oyj
Land = TBD
Name : ŽIVANEC, Mx. ÉLVA-NÖRI
Tel : <mailto:ELVA@VASKIVIRE.EXAMPLE>

Output:
{"name":"Élva-Nöri Živanec","phone":"+358416729385","email":"elva@vaskivire.example","company":"Vaskivire","country":"FI"}
